ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a standard feedback control block diagram: the input signal enters a summing point, the forward path is the block G(s), the output end is directly led out, and at the same time the output returns to the summing point through a feedback branch without an additional transfer function; the feedback end is marked with a minus sign, so this is a unity negative feedback system. Reasoning: For a unity negative feedback system, steady-state error can be judged using static error constants. Given the open-loop transfer function G(s) = (s+1)/(s^p(s+2)(s+3)), where the number of poles at the origin is p, that is, the system type is p. The steady-state error for a unit step input is 0, requiring the system to be at least type 1, so p >= 1. The steady-state error for a unit ramp input is a finite nonzero value 6, which only a type 1 system satisfies, therefore p = 1. Verification: When p = 1, Kv = lim_{s->0} sG(s) = lim_{s->0} (s+1)/((s+2)(s+3)) = 1/6, so the unit ramp steady-state error e_ss = 1/Kv = 6, consistent with the problem statement.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify a unity negative-feedback system, so use standard static error constants for the given open-loop transfer function. From the text, take G(s) = (s+1)/(s^p(s+2)(s+3)), with integer p, and the given errors: step error 0 and ramp error 6. The number of pure integrators in G(s) is p. Zero step error implies p >= 1. A finite nonzero unit-ramp error implies the system must be type 1, so p = 1. Verify the ramp value: Kv = lim_{s->0} sG(s) = lim_{s->0} (s+1)/((s+2)(s+3)) = 1/6, hence e_ss,ramp = 1/Kv = 6, confirming p = 1.

method.method_draft: From the image, model the loop as unity negative feedback, giving E(s)=R(s)/(1+G(s)). From the text, substitute G(s)=(s+1)/(s^p(s+2)(s+3)). For a unit step, e_ss = lim_{s->0} 1/(1+G(s)); the stated value 0 requires G(s)->infinity at s=0, so p must be positive. For a unit ramp, e_ss = lim_{s->0} 1/[s(1+G(s))]. Since sG(s)=(s+1)/(s^{p-1}(s+2)(s+3)), if p=1 the limit becomes 1/(1/6)=6; if p>1 the ramp error would be 0, and if p<=0 the step condition fails. Therefore the only integer p satisfying both stated errors is p=1.
